standard.title: Initiate, sustain and extend exchanges
standard.description: initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in a range of contexts, responding to ideas, opinions and perspectives about their own and others' personal worlds
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges in culturally appropriate ways across digital and social contexts (AC9LCH8EC01). They can manage invitations, personal exchanges, and online interaction. They have not yet extended exchanges into debate and argument contexts, used hypothetical and spontaneous role-play scenarios, or responded formally in professional or institutional communication contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in a range of contexts — including debate, formal online communication, hypothetical scenarios, and professional interaction — responding analytically to ideas, opinions and perspectives.

nodes.label: Debate strategies and reasoned argument
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply effective debate strategies — summarising key information, presenting balanced arguments, acknowledging and challenging others' views — in structured and semi-structured discussion.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a structured debate or discussion using at least two debate strategies (summarising, acknowledging, counter-arguing, or evidence use) and sustaining a reasoned position for at least four turns.
nodes.typical_width: Apply debate strategies; summarise key information and present balanced arguments; acknowledge strengths in others' ideas and provide contradicting evidence; share opinions on school-related and community topics linking ideas to support a view; engage with educational social media to document experiences.
wider: Lead a structured debate — facilitating argument, managing challenge, and bringing the discussion to a substantiated conclusion
Compare debate conventions in the target language community with Australian academic debate conventions — identify differences in how evidence, authority and disagreement are managed
nodes.hinge_reason: Debate and argument strategies are the prerequisite for all high-level exchange work at Y9-10. Students who can only assert opinions without reasoned argument cannot meet the analytical and advocacy demands this descriptor and the broader Y9-10 band require.

response_modes.reason: Debate strategies require students to construct and deploy reasoned arguments — not only express views. Explicit strategy instruction followed by practice in genuinely contested discussions builds the argumentative capacity needed.

success_criteria: Uses at least two debate strategies during a structured discussion
Sustains a reasoned position for at least four turns

nodes.label: Hypothetical and spontaneous interaction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in spontaneous and hypothetical role-plays — unfamiliar or unexpected scenarios — using target language flexibly without pre-prepared scripts.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one spontaneous or hypothetical role-play scenario without a pre-prepared script, sustaining the interaction for at least four turns.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in spontaneous hypothetical role-plays — seeing a doctor, handling personal emergencies, dealing with unfamiliar situations; sustain face-to-face and online conversations using strategies to prompt feedback; respond to open-ended questions without preparation.
wider: Participate in a series of progressively more unfamiliar hypothetical scenarios — identify which language resources transferred and which required improvisation
Reflect on the cognitive demands of spontaneous target language interaction — compare with prepared performance and discuss the strategies that help bridge the gap

response_modes.reason: Spontaneous interaction requires a bank of flexible language resources — strategies for managing unfamiliar situations, filler expressions, clarification moves — built through varied unscripted practice contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students who use the target language in real community contexts may already have spontaneous interaction experience. Width investment here extends this to formal and professional scenarios — building the range of registers available for spontaneous deployment.
success_criteria: Participates in a spontaneous role-play without a pre-prepared script
Sustains the interaction for at least four turns

nodes.label: Formal and professional communication
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond formally in professional or institutional contexts — job applications, formal correspondence, apology and gratitude conventions — using appropriate register.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one formal response to a real or simulated professional context (job advertisement, formal invitation, or institutional enquiry) using appropriate register throughout.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to personal letters, emails and job advertisements; express apology, appreciation and gratitude in diverse ways; compare practices across contexts; write formal correspondence for professional purposes; interact in professional or institutional contexts using appropriate conventions.
wider: Compare formal communication conventions across target language and Australian English professional contexts — identify differences in register markers, structural conventions and sign-off formulas
Draft a formal communication for a real professional purpose — apply target language formal conventions and evaluate against a model

response_modes.reason: Formal communication integrates argument and debate skills (node 1) and spontaneous interaction capacity (node 2) into a written professional register. The teaching investment is in creating genuine professional-context tasks — real job advertisements, real institutional scenarios — that require authentic formal register.

success_criteria: Produces a formal response using appropriate register throughout
Applies at least two formal register conventions for the specified context
